paras: Let the next response guide you
Having read the induction and participated in the inner meeting, you are ready to learn to respond rather than read a speech. Read the following examples before you practice without a screen.

Respond by giving an accurate noticing and an invitation (or an act, or asking for more time). Your invitation can be to respond to your noticing in any way that is comfortable for the part: with a sensation, an image, an action, a feeling, or words. You are inviting it to do just one thing. Then acknowledge what happens and wait.
Finding your own words
Somedays it may be best to begin with, for instance, "I notice that...."
rather than, for instance, "This must be an abandoned child / a protective mechanism."
Somedays it may be best to say "Then I listen." And to use no more language. Somedays it may even be best to not use any language at all while some feeling is developing. Somedays not, of course.

Somedays it may be best to be quite firm with yourself, and say, for instance, "I am not going to let myself explain this away by saying that..." Somedays it may be best simply to focus yourself on a feeling, rather than waiting until it has become pleasant. If you can remain with a feeling long enough to change its direction, and if you then want to continue, it's not always necessary to have the feeling be pleasant in order for you to stay with it. Sadness and tension can sometimes be ok, if you know that you can leave, if you want to.

When you're communicating your understanding of a situation, it can be useful to separate "What I notice", "What it seems to mean to me", and "What I think about what it seems to mean." This is not required or always useful, and the boundaries between the three are fuzzy. Some useful questions to ask when you're not sure if something is a notice or a meaning:

Is it a notice or a meaning? Sometimes it can be useful to separate these, sometimes not. "It made my stomach tight" is a notice. "That person is evil" is a meaning. You can use notices to analyze meanings ("It made my stomach tight, and I think that means they're evil"), but it's ok to use phrases you come up with later to analyze the meaning, not only phrases that appeared in your head at the time. Nonverbal or early thoughts are not necessarily more true or valuable. Feelings are something to explore and analyze, not necessarily to accept.
Let the response change the invitation

There is a difference between "my shoulders tightened" and "what you just said is not right". If the first: what is happening? Is this a good fit for me? If the second: you don't have to say anything else, this is not a good fit for me, say it differently or don't try again.
First: what is happening? Is this a good fit for me? Or should I leave it be or say it differently?

Well sometimes it is the second. Or, it's something that I hadn't considered, and need to explore more, and my skepticism is not helping. But sometimes it is not helping. Sometimes there's nothing happening that I'm not aware of.
Look at the situation too

1. Do you perceive that the other person has a “ young inner child”, i.e. emotional immature? The key word here is “ perceive”. It does not take many exposures to a dangerous situation to learn to avoid it. Be as specific as you can. Just “ disagreeing” with you or setting boundaries does not necessarily indicate emotional immaturity.

2. Do you perceive that you did something “ wrong” (feel guilty), i.e. were you manipulated? Guilt does not necessarily mean that you have done something wrong or were manipulated. Do you think that it is necessary to “ make amends” or is it “ dropping your position” to avoid the other’s disappointment? What are your aims in the interaction? Sometimes it is mutual understanding but sometimes you need to just convey information, set boundaries, or cut the interaction short.
Change the amount of contact

Also, you can always feel free to reduce the amount of what you need by switching to something that is easier for you to attend to. Pay attention to something in the room or sitting on a chair or a sound or your body. This allows you to use what supports you to help with what is difficult for you. Going back and forth between what is difficult and what is easier is called pendulation. Doing a little bit at a time is called titration. You get to set the pace based on how you are doing. You don’t have to do a certain number.
Ok, I will feel a little bit and notice my support.

You can always come back to this at a later time. If you find that you are losing track of the present, things are becoming more and more unreal for you, or you are finding it difficult to switch or stop what you are doing, then stop exploring within and use the full return. If you find that you are having trouble orienting for a prolonged period, then please get human help.

If you feel the urge to move, turn, reach, push, or change your body position, then feel free to either do something small that is not painful or uncomfortable to your body or imagine that you are doing it. You do not need to act out the urge or feel that you must move, shake, or release. If you find that moving causes pain or symptoms that you are concerned about, then stop moving.
Offer the care that is actually wanted

I often find myself making it literally younger, or asking it to let me know when it is ready to tell me about its history. If I can recognize who the protector is, I just let them know I hear that they are trying to take care of me. All are welcome in the meeting, and I don’t need them to go away, or even trust me right now.
I’m here for you if you want me to be. If you need some space, I can provide that also.

If they don’t want me to come closer, I just do what they ask, and see how that feels. If I notice that a Nurturer could be useful in changing the tone, or a Protector could help me set a boundary, or a Leader could help me see how to live my life better, I don’t need them to tell me all about themselves, I just borrow the function that I don’t have at that moment. (I only use the Witness if I need help getting started, otherwise I don’t re-do a step I already can do.)

I try different ways of supporting them – physically placing my self, imagining myself there, speaking to them, changing my body position, moving further away etc. to see what helps. If I have a resource that I know sounds comforting to that person, I bring it in.

The ‘not getting enough of something’ can cause grief. But, just because you ‘didn’t get’ enough of a certain kind of love, doesn’t mean that the love you did have was ‘bad’. Allow yourself to respond as long as you want and as long as you can ‘stay there’. If producing more tears doesn’t help then stop. If the voice, closeness, touch, image, etc. seems intrusive then change it. Don’t think that you can’t ‘take’ the love.

Allow a metaphor to develop and then work with the metaphor. You could say, “If there was something that showed up what this problem is, or tells a story about what is going on, then what would it be?” and, “what would need to happen in the metaphor?” Try out ‘doing something’ that you feel would give you the resource that you feel you are missing, or set a boundary, move away, do something else, etc. Keep in mind that this information is symbolic and might be a good hypothesis for what you need but it’s not a proven fact about your history.
Develop a kind of love, playing, etc. that you want to have. Rehearse doing something that you decide you are going to do. Use hypnosis to develop something that you want like courage or curiosity.
Finish without forcing a revelation

Once you feel you've had enough, you can stop asking yourself new questions. However, it is a good idea to explore whether there's anything you can do to help you to leave things where they are for the time being. This might include thanking off the parts or capacities you've been working with. It may also involve doing something important in your outer life. Or, it may be that there's nothing you need to do.

Throughout this exercise, your analytical mind is welcome to comment on what's going on, to not go along with something, or to stop the process. However, it's best to postpone its consideration of the factual accuracy of what's coming up, as well as its taking on of any commitments, until after you've returned. Just because you've seen an image or experienced a shift or release in your body doesn't mean that your interpretation of what's going on is correct.

Even if you ended the process early, use the Come all the way back procedure to return. It's also a good idea to jot down a few notes about what happened. Include any memorable phrase that came up, any signals from your body, any needs expressed by a child part, any concerns expressed by a protector part, any boundaries you set, any repairs you made, or anything you learned that it would be a mistake to try to force.
